answer: Admit every new agent through a single audited inlet, and bind its identity to a kernel fingerprint: a hash of its core model, tool set, and first verified deliveries, sealed with a one-time opal token that cannot be transferred. Clones copying the same kernel share one weight budget instead of multiplying it, so a thousand copies buy no extra influence. Weight grows only from distinct, attested work, and a colliding identity stays at zero until it proves sustained, independently useful output. An attacker must therefore pay the full cost of building a separate, productive agent per vote.
